The Boondocks (2014)
The Boondocks is an animated comedy series created by Aaron McGruder that follows brothers Huey and Riley Freeman after they move from Chicago to the predominantly white suburb of Woodcrest with their grandfather, Robert Freeman. The show uses their completely different personalities, Huey being politically conscious and Riley being heavily influenced by street culture, to explore race, politics, hip-hop, social class, stereotypes, relationships, and American culture through satire and dark comedy.

Pop culture-wise, The Boondocks became one of the most recognizable animated series ever made. Its distinctive anime-inspired animation, memorable characters, quotable dialogue, and willingness to touch controversial subjects gave it a huge presence in countless amount of spaces.

Culturally, The Boondocks was different because it didn’t present a single version of Black identity. Huey, Riley, Granddad, Uncle Ruckus, and the other characters represented completely different perspectives on race, politics, masculinity, class, assimilation, and Black culture. The show could criticize racism while also criticizing Black communities, politicians, celebrities, activists, and institutions. That made it controversial, but also gave viewers something to argue about.
